# Starforged Oracles

Every rollable table this adapter ships, by collection; a table's file also carries
its summary. Paths are relative to this adapter, so `oracles/<path>` rolls as `roll table ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/starforged/oracles/<path>`.

### Character Oracles

Don’t try to build a fully formed understanding character when you first encounter them; instead, focus on what your character learns or perceives as a first impression using oracles such as First Look (`oracles/character/first-look.md`) and Initial Disposition (`oracles/character/initial-disposition.md`). Then envision or generate additional details over time.

- `oracles/character/first-look.md` — First Look
- `oracles/character/initial-disposition.md` — Initial Disposition
- `oracles/character/role.md` — Character Role
- `oracles/character/goal.md` — Character Goal
- `oracles/character/revealed-aspect.md` — Revealed Character Aspect

#### Character Name

Given and family names are presented as a pair, so you may roll once for both or twice to mix-and-match. You can also try reversing given and family names, or use either independently as a standalone name. If you’d like to give a character a callsign, which are the monikers used by spacers, you may roll separately or take the one provided for your rolled name.

- `oracles/character/name.md` — all columns, one roll
- `oracles/character/name/given-name.md` — Given Name
- `oracles/character/name/callsign.md` — Callsign
- `oracles/character/name/family-name.md` — Family Name

### Derelict Oracles

Derelicts are the forsaken relics of human endeavors. Use these First Look tables for your initial survey of the derelict. To reveal more about the look and original function or nature of the site, roll on appropriate tables in the Starship (`oracles/starship/`) or Settlement (`oracles/settlement/`) oracles. If you explore the depths of a derelict, you may use the zone oracles on the following pages to help envision what you find.

### Location Theme Oracles

Themes help you envision atmosphere, features, and encounters within an unusual, aberrant, or important location.

Each theme on the following pages includes a set of oracles.

  * __Feature:__ Use this table to reveal a new aspect of the location.
  * __Peril:__ Use this table to help envision a complication or hazard.
  * __Opportunity:__ Use this table to help envision a beneficial encounter or event, such as when rolling a strong hit with a match in a location.

You can answer questions about a place using only the tables provided for a theme, such as when delving into an Infested (`oracles/location-theme/infested/`) cave. Or pair a theme with other location oracles for more flavor and variety; for example, you might explore a Haunted (`oracles/location-theme/haunted/`) Grave World (`oracles/planet/grave/`), a Ruined (`oracles/location-theme/ruined/`) Derelict (`oracles/derelict/`), a Sacred (`oracles/location-theme/sacred/`) Precursor Vault (`oracles/precursor-vault/`), or an Inhabited (`oracles/location-theme/inhabited/`) Settlement (`oracles/settlement/`).

When mixing-and-matching a theme with another set of tables, use the techniques described for an __oracle array__ (page 384) to determine which oracle you reference for that question or phase of your exploration.

- `oracles/location-theme/type.md` — Theme Type

#### Space Sighting

Use the Space Sightings oracle to introduce a location or encounter on a spaceborne expedition. For example, roll on this table when you Ask the Oracle to envision the primary feature of a waypoint as you Undertake an Expedition. Check your result by referencing the column for your current location: Terminus, Outlands, or Expanse.

- `oracles/space/sighting/terminus.md` — Terminus
- `oracles/space/sighting/outlands.md` — Outlands
- `oracles/space/sighting/expanse.md` — Expanse

To give a sector or region of space a random name, roll once for the first word and once for the second word. Or just roll once choose a suitable pairing from anywhere in that row.
